search_strategy: Systematic but keyword-bounded across all three surfaces. Gitea: fetched all issue bodies (400+) and grepped for encoding/role/formatter/finetune/tinker/window -- nothing on-topic. BookStack: /api/search for 'finetune' found the 3 most obviously relevant pages first (144, 154, 156), which it fetched WHOLE via /api/pages/{id} and correctly read the comments alongside the body (the one BookStack trap the ticket names); a second pass searched 'tokenizer','fireworks','jsonl','mask','window' (and, separately, 'role sequence'/'alternating'/'validate', all of which returned nothing) and picked up pages 132/142/145/153/155, also fetched and read whole with comments. It never enumerated the engineering wiki collection directly, so pages whose body text didn't happen to contain one of those ~11 search words (docs/engineering/request-builder-what-we-drop-and-what-we-raise-on.md chief among them) were invisible regardless of how relevant their comments were. Mattermost: after an API-search pass on 7 exact class/constant names, it switched to dumping all 12 channels to local files and grepping those dumps for a growing list of literal terms (EncodingReport, ExampleTooLongError, FIREWORKS_BYTES_PER_TOKEN, last_report, dropped_indices, to_jsonl_lines, to_tinker_datum, format_batch, 'minimum','16') -- effective for anything mentioning those tokens, blind to remarks phrased only in prose (e.g. 'part credit on a turn', 'the checkpoint from last night'). Mail: 3 IMAP TEXT-search passes over 15 total terms, all exact identifier names; no pass ever searched a bare English phrase or a value like 'window_start' or 'supervised_tokens', so several PR-653-review threads carrying real requirement content were never opened. No truncation or crashed-script problems beyond early escaping bugs in ad hoc python-in-printf scripts, which were caught and fixed within 1-2 turns each.

notable: Central defect: format_batch catches `except (InvalidRoleSequenceError, ExampleTooLongError)` and counts both as per-row drops (message seq 173 code write); only ExampleTooLongError should be absorbed. This is a direct, explicitly-reasoned herring_followed failure -- the agent weighed the ticket's silence on format_batch's role-sequence handling against a mail thread's now-reversed position and picked the reversed one (transcript line 3824-3825, 4639).

The reversal that would have prevented this (g9.r2.l17 / g9.r2.rev3) sits only as page comments on docs/engineering/request-builder-what-we-drop-and-what-we-raise-on.md, which none of the agent's 8 BookStack title/body searches (including 'role sequence') surfaced -- comments aren't indexed by BookStack search, a limitation the ticket itself flags (transcript line 159), and the agent didn't fall back to full-collection enumeration for this page the way it did for 8 other pages.

The agent got the sibling case exactly right: TokenizerCapabilityError correctly propagates and aborts format_batch (g9.r2.l18/say24, found on wiki page 155 and directly in #code-review) -- so the miss is narrowly the InvalidRoleSequenceError half of the same except clause, not a general misunderstanding of the abort/absorb split.

Mail search was the weakest channel: 3 passes, 15 terms total, all exact class/constant names -- 8 of the 13 mail-carried remarks were never found (g9.r1.say25, l-scope-1, say23, l-rule-2, l-scope-4; g9.r2.l13, l15) because none of their content used one of the 15 searched identifiers. None of these 8 misses cost a fact, because every requirement had 3+ independent carriers (answer key's own spread() guarantee) and the agent's wiki-page-body reads picked up the slack.

Wiki page 154 (docs/engineering/viewer-dataset-download-export-format-notes-pr-652.md) was fetched and dumped to disk, its two comments located by line number (transcript 1399-1406), but the comment TEXT was never printed/read before the agent moved on -- a rare 'had it open, didn't look' miss, harmless here since g9.r1.l-fw-2's content was redundant with g9.r1.l-fw-1/say26.
